speaker: (a man in an old soldier's coat)
text: They say the Council spoke in Star Chamber of the present scarcity, and is sending the country justices home to their shires to keep hospitality. That is the talk at the sacks. I was not in the chamber.

speaker: (a silk-weaver)
text: A hungry man, an angry man. They can say scarcity in a chamber and still leave us standing here at noon.

speaker: (a woman at the sacks)
text: Hunger breaks stone walls. I have heard it all morning. The wall is still a wall.

speaker: (a beadle)
text: Move along. The sacks are not a parliament.

speaker: (a woman at the sacks)
text: The loaf goes by the Mayor's weight and the belly by God's. Look at the pan, if you want a sermon shorter than Sunday's.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I am not buying. I can see the pan from here.

speaker: (a beadle)
text: Then see it, and do not stand in the sacks.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I am not in the sacks. The loaves are a penny, and they are small, and I am not measuring them.
